name: Fauvism
region: Paris and the south coast of France
summary: Colour at full strength and not true to nature: a green face, an orange sky. Flat patches, bold contours and quick strokes make the picture an arrangement of colour first.

philosophy.core_thesis: Colour is free from the object: the painter chooses a hue for its force and its relations, and so builds the picture and the feeling by colour alone.
design_principles: Choose each hue for its force and not for its likeness: a green shadow, a red tree, a blue face.
Apply the colour pure, straight from the tube, in large flat patches of 30–200mm.
Set strong contrasts of complementary pairs at full saturation: red against green, orange against blue.
Outline the forms in a dark or coloured contour of 3–10mm, and leave the area inside flat.
Flatten the space: reduce the depth to 1–2 layers and let the colour carry the distance.
Paint fast, with a visible brush stroke, and leave bare ground between patches.
Take plain subjects, such as a landscape, a port, a portrait and a bather, and show them in bold, simple shapes.
anti_patterns: Blended, graded modelling that makes a round form
Fine, fussy detail and a polished surface
Dots or a scientific system of colour

composition.layout: Large flat colour shapes with a bold contour, in a shallow space of 1–2 layers; the shapes divide the picture into 5–12 patches.
composition.focal_point: The strongest colour contrast, a complementary pair, at about one third from an edge, in a patch at 10–20% of the area.
composition.format: A canvas at 4:5 to 3:2, with the subject cut by the edge; a figure fills 50–80% of the height.

principles.rule: Set one complementary pair, such as red against green, at full saturation in the main patch, with a hue shift of 150° or more.
Divide the picture in 4–6 pure hue patches of 10–25% each, with no hue lower than 5% and none above 30%.
Reduce the depth to 1–2 layers, and show distance by colour temperature, not by size or haze.
Repeat a stroke or a curve 8–15 times at 20–60mm, so that the colour patches move across the picture.
Hold one contour weight of 3–10mm and one stroke width, and let the hue vary from patch to patch.
Make the face or the main shape the largest, brightest patch at one third from an edge, and keep the rest 10–15% lower in value.

palette.strategy: Pure, saturated hues used for force and not for likeness, in strong complementary pairs, with a dark contour and bare ground.
palette.distribution: 4–6 hue patches at 10–25% each, bare or white ground 5–15%, dark contour under 10%.
palette.ground: A white ground that is left bare in places and lifts the colour.

colours.name: Emerald green
colours.role: complement of the red; a face shadow

brushwork_and_medium.medium: Oil paint straight from the tube, thick, with little or no thinner.
brushwork_and_medium.support: Canvas with a white ground, in small and medium sizes.
brushwork_and_medium.brushwork: Broad, quick strokes of 15–40mm, short, straight or curved, with a few thin lines of 3–10mm for contour.
brushwork_and_medium.paint_handling: One layer, rarely two; the patches are flat and opaque, with a gap of bare ground between them.
brushwork_and_medium.edges: A hard, dark or coloured contour at 3–10mm on the main forms; the colour patches meet with a ragged edge.

light_and_modelling.light: No single source: the light is in the colour, and a patch of high-key colour is the light.
light_and_modelling.modelling: Little or none; a form turns by a change of hue from warm to cool, in 1–2 steps.
light_and_modelling.shadow: A colour and not a dark: green, violet or blue patch at the same value as its neighbour.
light_and_modelling.temperature: Chosen for feeling and for contrast; warm patches next to cool ones, with a hue shift of 150° or more.

subject.typical: Port and harbour scenes, a sunlit landscape, a portrait, a bather, a still life and an interior with a window.
subject.figure_scale: A figure fills 50–80% of the picture height, or a landscape fills the whole canvas.
subject.treatment: Direct, joyful and simple; the subject is a reason for colour, and the face is a patch like any other.

surface.finish: Matt to semi-gloss with a bare, raw look.
surface.texture: Flat patches with a visible brush ridge, and bare canvas that shows between.

reference_works.note: Object ids were checked against the Art Institute of Chicago API (CC0 data). Two works are not flagged as public domain by the museum: the ids identify them only. Look at the museum page for the image and its licence; do not copy it.

emotion.target_response: Exhilaration and heat: the viewer is struck by colour first and feels the joy of a bright day.

use_cases: poster, festival and summer campaign art
packaging for drinks, food and sport
editorial illustration with a bold palette
avoid_when: The brief needs a muted, serious or luxury calm.
The picture must show true product colour.

modifiers.how: Keep the pure hue and the complementary pairs; break each patch into dots of 2–5mm, add a still frieze layout and a painted border.
Keep the flat patches; cut the palette to 3–4 earth hues, break the subject into tilted planes, and show more than one viewpoint.

value_contrast.note: Fauve colour works by hue, not by dark and light, so the value span stays moderate.

sources.title: Art Institute of Chicago API (CC0 data)
Henri Matisse, Notes of a Painter (La Grande Revue, 1908)
